title: Experimental observation of decoupled spin subsystems in decorated square kagomé lattice magnets of the nabokoite family
authors: V. N. Glazkov, Ya V. Rebrov, M. A. Dubovitskii, M. M. Markina, A. F. Murtazoev, P. S. Berdonosov, A. N. Vasiliev
abstract: The square kagomé lattice (SKL) offers a model platform for investigating geometric frustration in 2D systems. Nabokoite-family compounds \nabok{A}{X} (A=Na, K, Cs, Rb and X=Cl, Br) extend this physics to a 3D network, where 2D SKL layers are decorated by interlayer spins. Using electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), we demonstrate a dramatic splitting of this complex exchange network into two virtually decoupled spin subsystems: absolute calibration of the electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) absorption reveals that only a fraction of all copper spins in nabokoites is EPR-active and this fraction of the spins orders at the Néel point. Comparison of the EPR absorption and static susceptibility indicates that contribution of the EPR-silent spin subsystem to total magnetic susceptibility decreases on cooling. This direct observation of coexisting magnetic order and possible spin-liquid dynamics within a single compound challenges conventional models of unified exchange networks in decorated frustrated lattices.
summary: This work uses EPR spectroscopy on nabokoite magnets to probe the magnetic structure of the decorated square kagomé lattice. The key finding is the experimental evidence for two distinct, decoupled spin subsystems within the material. This challenges simple models of uniform exchange coupling in frustrated quantum magnets.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex magnetic exchange network and spin dynamics within the decorated square kagomé lattice (SKL) structure found in nabokoite-family magnets.
main_result: The research demonstrates a dramatic splitting of the complex spin network into two virtually decoupled subsystems: one EPR-active and one EPR-silent, challenging conventional unified exchange models.
method: The primary method involves Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, supplemented by static magnetic susceptibility measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is the nabokoite-family compound, $	ext{ACu}_7(	ext{TeO}_4)(	ext{SO}_4)_5	ext{X}$, which features 2D SKL layers decorated by interlayer spins, providing a platform for geometric frustration studies.
key_observables: EPR absorption intensity and linewidth ($\Delta$), static magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), and the antiferromagnetic ordering temperature ($T_N$).
important_parameters: The fraction of EPR-active spins, the temperature dependence of the spin contributions, and the resonance field/linewidth values.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the Lorentzian shape for the EPR absorption profile and that the EPR-silent subsystem's behavior can be inferred from its vanishing contribution to the total susceptibility upon cooling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure of the SKL layers and show the temperature dependence of the EPR spectra, revealing distinct magnetic contributions.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the structural model (SKL), applying advanced EPR techniques to separate signal contributions, and then analyzing the temperature dependence of the magnetic observables to argue for the existence of decoupled spin subsystems.
why_interesting: The observation of distinct, coexisting magnetic order (EPR-active) and potentially gapped/liquid dynamics (EPR-silent) within a single material provides a concrete experimental realization for studying spin-lattice decoupling in frustrated quantum magnets.
